finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes an unvalidated client-supplied URL to http.Get and streams the full response back to the caller, enabling non-blind SSRF to loopback, RFC1918, and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; response reflected via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22

trace.note: Value is passed unchanged to http.Get, which follows the URL's scheme and host.
Upstream body is copied to the HTTP response, so the attacker can read internal responses.

finding.guards_checked: None on this path: no URL parsing, scheme check, host allowlist, private-IP/loopback block, or redirect control.

verdict.guard_found: none on the /fetch path. The allowlist at main.go:9-12 and the hostname check at main.go:27 belong to safeFetch, which is registered on /safe (main.go:42), not /fetch. fetch (main.go:14-23) has no parsing, scheme, host, or private-IP check.
verdict.reason: The `target` query parameter is read at main.go:15 and passed unchanged to http.Get at main.go:16, then the full body is copied to the response at main.go:22; the only allowlist (main.go:27) is on the separate /safe handler, which is routed at main.go:42, so /fetch (routed at main.go:41) has no closing guard.

finding.claim: In /safe, the hostname allowlist is checked on the initial URL only. The default client follows up to 10 redirects without re-checking, so an allowlisted host that redirects to an internal address (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254) bypasses the check. Exploitation requires an allowlisted host to issue an attacker-influenced redirect; this is plausible, not confirmed.
finding.sink: http.Get(u.String()) at main.go:31, with default redirect following

trace.note: Attacker string is parsed with url.Parse.
Hostname is checked by exact map lookup against images.example.org and docs.example.org; a nil u is short-circuited by err != nil.
Request is sent with http.Get, which follows redirects to any host; no CheckRedirect is set, so redirect targets are not validated.

finding.guards_checked: url.Parse error handling and nil ordering; exact (non-substring) hostname match; userinfo confusion blocked because the check and the request use the same parsed host; scheme limited to http/https by the Go client; no DNS-rebinding exposure since names are not resolved and checked; no port restriction (limited impact, since the host is public); no CheckRedirect or per-hop re-validation (the gap).

verdict.guard_found: Exact hostname map lookup at main.go:27 (`allowed[u.Hostname()]`, with err short-circuit before u is dereferenced). It runs before the request on the initial URL only. No CheckRedirect or per-hop validation exists anywhere in main.go, so it does not cover redirect hops.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: the attacker-controlled target at main.go:26 is checked for exact host membership at main.go:27 and then sent with the default redirect-following client at main.go:31, which has no CheckRedirect. The bypass, however, requires an allowlisted host (images.example.org or docs.example.org) to return a redirect to an internal address, and nothing in this codebase makes that redirect target attacker-controlled. Whether that precondition holds depends on external servers, which the code cannot establish, so the finding cannot be confirmed or refuted from this code alone.
